glosses: Used other than figuratively or idiomatically: see get, in.
To get into or inside something, literally or figuratively.

examples.text: Hurry up and get in the car!
He tried to go after the ball but couldn't get in the game.
You'd better get in gear. We've got work to do!

glosses: To enter a place; to gain access.

examples.text: If you want to get in, you'll need the gate code and a key.
Teens walk the redlight district but can never get in.
They hacked his password and finally got in.

glosses: To secure membership at a selective school.

examples.text: All of our students who applied to university got in.

glosses: To be elected to some office.

examples.text: Do the early results say our candidate will get in?

glosses: To become dark earlier as a result of seasonal change; to draw in.

examples.text: Winter's on the way, and the nights are getting in.

glosses: To arrive.

examples.text: What time does your flight get in?
It was gone 9 o'clock by the time I got in from work last night.

glosses: Synonym of drive out (To take up less space because the typesetter uses type that is thinner than the copy or the typesetter whites out more or squeezes in more lines on each page.)

An exclamation of joy at one's success.

examples.text:

- Get in!

examples.text: «Por horas, el tubito va de izquierda a derecha, la punta sube, baja, tiembla, remolonea sobre el papel y va drenando un hilo azul sobre las líneas grises».

examples.text: «Los dos palurdos pasan por una puerta de cristales negros, suben por una escalera de metal y se encuentran en un salón hundido en la oscuridad, animado con luces intermitentes».

examples.text: «El amanecer me disipó los malos sueños. La temperatura empezaba a subir hasta los 45 grados. Transpirábamos en abundancia, pero el sudor se evaporaba instantáneamente».
